question: Who headed the Diwan-i-Arz and was responsible for managing soldiers, branding horses, and administering war provisions?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Naib
Amir-i-Dad
Ariz-i-Mumalik
Dabir-i-Khas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ariz-i-Mumalik

Explanation:
In the administrative system of the Delhi Sultanate, the head of the Diwan-i-Arz was called Ariz-i-Mumalik. This department was responsible for military affairs, including recruitment, salary, and discipline of soldiers. The Diwan-i-Arz also managed the branding of horses (dagh) and the muster roll (talika) of soldiers. During wars, it handled weapons, logistics, and food supply. The Ariz-i-Mumalik was accountable directly to the Sultan and played a crucial role in maintaining the army's strength. This position was highly prestigious in the Sultanate period.

question: During the expansion of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, which of the following cities became the capital of Vatsaraja?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Ujjain
Mathura
Kannauj
Malwa
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ujjain

Explanation:
During the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, Vatsaraja (c. 780-800 CE) expanded the kingdom. He made Ujjain his capital, an important city in the Malwa region. Vatsaraja fought against the Pala king Dharmapala and the Rashtrakuta king Dhruva. Although later rulers shifted the capital to Kannauj, during Vatsaraja's reign Ujjain was the main center. Ujjain is an ancient city and part of Malwa region, but Malwa is a region, not a city. Mathura and Kannauj were also in Pratihara territory, but Vatsaraja's capital was Ujjain.

Explanation:

question: Babur, the first Mughal ruler, was related to two of the medieval world's greatest conquerors. If he was related to the Mongol conqueror Genghis Khan on his maternal side, to whom was he related on his paternal side?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Mohammed Ghori
Mahmud Ghazni
Timur
Ibrahim Lodi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Timur

Explanation:
Babur was the founder of the Mughal dynasty. On his maternal side, his mother Qutlugh Nigar Khanum was the daughter of Yunus Khan, a Mongol ruler descended from Genghis Khan, making Babur a descendant of Genghis Khan. On his paternal side, Babur was related to Timur (Timur Lang), as his father Umar Sheikh Mirza was a great-grandson of Timur. Timur was a Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire in 1370 CE. Babur established the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 CE. Thus, Babur was a descendant of two of the greatest medieval conquerors: Genghis Khan and Timur, giving him a strong lineage and legacy.

☛ When was the First Battle of Panipat fought? → 1526 CE
question_hi: प्रथम मुगल शासक बाबर, मध्यकालीन विश्व के दो सबसे बड़े विजेताओं से संबंधित था। यदि वह मातृपक्ष में मंगोल विजेता चंगेज खान से संबंधित था, तो पितृपक्ष में वह किससे संबंधित था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: मोहम्मद गौरी
महमूद गजनी
तैमूर
इब्राहिम लोदी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है तैमूर

Explanation:
बाबर मुगल वंश का संस्थापक था। उसकी माता कुतलुग निगार खानम चंगेज खान के वंशज मंगोल शासक यूनुस खान की पुत्री थी, जिससे वह मातृपक्ष में चंगेज खान से संबंधित था। पितृपक्ष में बाबर का संबंध तैमूर (तैमूर लंग) से था, क्योंकि उसके पिता उमर शेख मिर्जा तैमूर के परपोते थे। तैमूर एक तुर्क-मंगोल विजेता था जिसने 1370 ई. में तैमूरी साम्राज्य की स्थापना की। बाबर ने 1526 ई. में पानीपत के प्रथम युद्ध में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराकर भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी। इस प्रकार बाबर दो महान विजेताओं चंगेज खान और तैमूर का वंशज था, जिसने उसे एक मजबूत विरासत दी।

question: Rajendra Chola I is known for his naval expeditions on the revived Sri Vijaya empire of:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Which foreign ruler invaded India in 1739, leading to the massacre of Delhi and further weakening the Mughal Empire?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sher Shah
Ahmad Shah Abdali
Nadir Shah
Babur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nadir Shah

Explanation:
Nadir Shah was the ruler of Persia (Iran) who invaded India in 1739. He defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal and entered Delhi. After a rebellion in Delhi, Nadir Shah ordered a brutal massacre that killed about 30,000 people. He looted the Peacock Throne and the Kohinoor diamond and took them to Persia. This invasion severely weakened the Mughal Empire, paving the way for further foreign invasions and the eventual decline of Mughal rule in India.

question_hi: किस विदेशी शासक ने 1739 में भारत पर आक्रमण किया, जिसके कारण दिल्ली का नरसंहार हुआ और मुगल साम्राज्य और कमजोर हो गया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 2)

question: On which of the following states of India did Siraj-ud- Daula, Mir Jafar and Mir Qasim rule in the 18th century? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Bengal
Andhra
Gujarat
Kerala
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bengal

Explanation:
In the 18th century, the three prominent Nawabs of Bengal were Siraj-ud-Daula (1756–1757), Mir Jafar (1757–1760), and Mir Qasim (1760–1763). Siraj-ud-Daula was the last independent Nawab of Bengal. He lost his throne after his defeat in the Battle of Plassey in 1757 against Robert Clive. Mir Jafar was installed as the Nawab by the East India Company, but later replaced by Mir Qasim. Mir Qasim faced defeat in the Battle of Buxar in 1764. All three rulers governed the Bengal region, which included present-day West Bengal, Bangladesh, and parts of Bihar.

question: Who fought the Battle of Plassey against the East India Company? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)

question: Who took away the Peacock Throne from India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Nadir Shah
Genghis Khan
Mohammad bin Tuglaq
Ahmed Shah
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nadir Shah

Explanation:
India's famous Peacock Throne was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. It was taken away by Nadir Shah, the ruler of Persia (Iran), when he invaded India in 1739 CE. Nadir Shah defeated Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah Rangeela in the Battle of Karnal and captured Delhi. He took the Peacock Throne, the Kohinoor diamond, and other treasures to Persia. The throne was known for two peacocks with a large diamond between them. No original version of the Peacock Throne exists today. Nadir Shah was assassinated by his own soldiers in 1747 CE. After his death, the Peacock Throne disappeared.

question: The noted traveller and writer Muhammad Ibn Battuta, who travelled to many countries including India in the 14th century, belonged to which of the following countries? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Morocco
Libya
Ghana
Algeria
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Morocco

Explanation:
Muhammad Ibn Battuta was born in 1304 CE in Tangier, Morocco, and is renowned as one of history's greatest travelers and writers. In the 14th century, he traveled over 1,20,000 kilometers, covering most of the Islamic world and beyond. He visited India in 1333 CE during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq of the Delhi Sultanate, where he served as a judge (Qazi). His travelogue, known as Rihla or My Travels, provides detailed accounts of India, China, the Maldives, and Africa. Ibn Battuta's writings are invaluable to historians for understanding medieval societies. He is widely regarded as the greatest medieval traveler.

question: The historical Grand Trunk road was developed by many rulers. What was it called during the reign of the Mauryas? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Uttarpath

Rajpath
Poorvipath
solution:

Explanation:
The historical Grand Trunk Road was called Uttarpath during the Mauryan period. This road was a major trade and military route in ancient India, connecting the eastern and western parts. The Mauryan rulers Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka developed and maintained this route. 'Uttarpath' means northern path. Later, Sher Shah Suri renamed it 'Badshahi Sadak', and the British called it Grand Trunk Road. 'Rajpath' and 'Poorvipath' are names of other ancient routes. During the Mauryan era, this route ran from Pataliputra to Taxila.
